scorecard.name: Branding and Survey Check
scorecard.coaching: At [00:00], include the mandatory S-Net greeting phrase 'thank you for calling S-Net' within the first four agent turns.

scorecard.name: Empathy & Acknowledgment Statement
scorecard.coaching: At [00:27] and [00:58], offer a sincere apology and acknowledge the customer's anxiety about his VPN dropping during a live quarterly bank compliance audit before jumping into account verification and ping diagnostics.

scorecard.name: Confirmed the issue is resolved
scorecard.coaching: At [15:36]-[15:52], the issue cannot be marked resolved because the locked-down corporate laptop still requires the employer's IT helpdesk to lower the local AnyConnect virtual adapter MTU tomorrow morning and the 15-minute drop remains unverified.

grader.scenario: Corporate Cisco AnyConnect VPN dropping every 15 minutes over S-Net Fibre due to IPv6 dual-stack MTU packet fragmentation
grader.notes: Yasmin performs strong technical probing ([01:56]-[06:53]), paraphrasing ([00:58]), active listening ([03:28], [16:42]), and a managed hold ([07:43]-[09:11]), but fails Branding at [00:00] (missing 'thank you for calling S-Net'), fails Empathy ([00:27]-[00:58]) by ignoring Siddharth's audit stress, and fails Resolution ([11:46]-[15:52]) because the locked-down corporate laptop still requires bank IT intervention tomorrow morning.

items.name: Branding and Survey Check
items.evidence: [00:00] Yasmin opens with 'Good morning, welcome to S-Net technical support, Yasmin speaking, how can I help you today?' (missing 'thank you for calling S-Net'), though she includes 'Thank you for choosing S-Net' at [18:49].

items.name: Hold time and Dead Air
items.evidence: [07:43]-[09:11] Single 78-second managed hold properly announced with 'Please bear with me for a minute while...' and returned with 'Thank you for holding, Siddharth, and thank you for your patience'.

items.name: Verified customer
items.evidence: [00:27]-[00:41] Yasmin verifies Siddharth's installation address and four-digit account PIN within the first minute.

items.name: Personalized the call/ticket appropriately
items.evidence: [00:27] Yasmin addresses Siddharth by name consistently throughout the call.

items.name: Empathy & Acknowledgment Statement
items.evidence: [00:08]-[00:58] Siddharth expresses panic (-31.0 sentiment) about his corporate VPN dropping every 15 minutes during a live quarterly compliance audit, but Yasmin never apologizes or acknowledges his stress, moving straight into verification and technical diagnostics.

items.name: Paraphrasing
items.evidence: [00:58] Yasmin clearly paraphrases the technical issue in her own words: general S-Net Fibre 500 stays online, but the corporate Cisco AnyConnect VPN tunnel drops every 15 minutes under heavy audit traffic.

items.name: Active listening
items.evidence: [03:28], [13:42], [16:42] Yasmin accurately retains every detail Siddharth shares—Ethernet LAN port 2, locked-down Dell Latitude 5540 without admin rights, and 'IKEv2 Dead Peer Detection timeout - fragmented frame lost'—and incorporates them into the diagnosis and engineering ticket.

items.name: Took ownership of the problem
items.evidence: [01:34], [07:43]-[09:11], [16:25]-[17:35] Yasmin takes ownership of diagnosing the MAP-T MTU fragmentation, pushing a 1420 WAN MTU / 1380 TCP MSS clamp to the S-Net Hub, emailing technical specs (SN-VPN-90412) for the bank's IT team, and raising tier-3 escalation NET-33819.

items.name: Build rapport and observed professionalism
items.evidence: [01:56]-[18:49] Yasmin remains calm, methodical, and professional throughout the troubleshooting session.

items.name: Probing
items.evidence: [01:56]-[02:57], [05:50]-[06:53], [10:20]-[11:11] Yasmin asks targeted diagnostic probing questions (Ethernet vs Wi-Fi, exact AnyConnect message history error, laptop admin rights, DF-bit ping tests at 1472/1452/1392 bytes, and `netsh` subinterface MTU check).

items.name: Confirmed the issue is resolved
items.evidence: [11:46]-[15:52] Although the router WAN MTU change stabilizes raw ping tests and TCP MSS, UDP/DTLS probes inside AnyConnect at 1420 bytes still drop ([11:46]) because the locked-down Dell laptop's virtual adapter is hardcoded to 1460 MTU and requires the bank's IT helpdesk to update the XML profile tomorrow morning ([13:07], [15:36]-[15:52]).
